verses.text: Abraham moved on from there into the Negev and lived between Kadesh and Shur. For a while he stayed in Gerar.
There Abraham said about his wife Sarah, "She is my sister." So Abimelech king of Gerar sent for Sarah and took her.
But God came to Abimelech in a dream one night and said to him, "You are as good as dead because of the woman you have taken. She is a married woman."
Now Abimelech had not gone near her. So he said, "Lord, will you destroy a nation that has done nothing wrong?
Did Abraham not say to me, 'She is my sister'? And did she not also say, 'He is my brother'? I did this with a clear conscience and clean hands."
Then God said to him in the dream, "Yes, I know you did this with a clear conscience. That is why I kept you from sinning against me. That is why I did not let you touch her.
Now give the man's wife back to him. He is a prophet, and he will pray for you, and you will live. But if you do not give her back, you can be sure that you and all your people will die."
Early the next morning Abimelech called all his officials together. When he told them everything that had happened, they were very afraid.

Then Abimelech called Abraham in and said, "What have you done to us? What wrong have I done to you, that you have brought such great guilt on me and my kingdom? You have done things to me that should never be done."
And Abimelech asked Abraham, "What were you thinking of when you did this?"
Abraham answered, "I said to myself, 'There is surely no fear of God in this place, and they will kill me because of my wife.'
Besides, she really is my sister. She is the daughter of my father, though not of my mother, and she became my wife.
When God sent me wandering away from my father's home, I said to her, 'This is how you can show your love for me: everywhere we go, say about me, "He is my brother."'"
Then Abimelech brought sheep and cattle and male and female slaves, and gave them to Abraham. And he gave his wife Sarah back to him.
Abimelech said, "My land is in front of you. Live wherever you like."
To Sarah he said, "I am giving your brother a thousand pieces of silver. This is to show everyone with you that you are innocent. Everyone will know that you have done nothing wrong."
Then Abraham prayed to God, and God healed Abimelech, his wife and his slave women, so that they could have children again.
The LORD had kept every woman in Abimelech's household from having children, because of Abraham's wife Sarah.
